class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make this repository ready for Muse Code. Add scripts/muse-exec.sh that checks `muse --version` (printing the one-line install command for this OS when muse is missing), then runs `muse exec &quot;$@&quot;` from the repo root so any prompt can run headless. Add a short &quot;Using Muse Code&quot; section to the README: install, first run (`muse` in the repo, trust the workspace, sign in with the browser or an API key, `/login` to reopen it) and META_API_KEY for CI. Don&#x27;t install anything or sign in yourself.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Muse Code&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows PowerShell); confirm with `muse --version`.
- `muse` starts a session. The first run asks to trust the workspace (that loads its skills, rules and hooks) and to sign in with a browser or an API key.
- `muse exec &quot;&lt;prompt&gt;&quot;` runs one prompt to completion. Without a browser, Muse Code reads META_API_KEY (not MODEL_API_KEY).
- The default model is muse-spark-1.2; `--model` overrides it per run.
- On Windows agent commands use PowerShell, voice input and session messaging are unavailable, and the sandbox may show a UAC prompt once.
- Programs can drive a session with `muse serve` (`muse schema` prints the protocol&#x27;s JSON schema) or `npm install @muse-code/sdk`.

Starter code (Python)
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

# Run one Muse Code prompt headless; the agent&#x27;s output comes back on stdout.
if shutil.which(&quot;muse&quot;) is None:
    sys.exit(&quot;Install Muse Code: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh&quot;)

prompt = &quot; &quot;.join(sys.argv[1:]) or &quot;Summarize this repo.&quot;
run = subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, prompt], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(run.stdout)
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec exited {run.returncode}: {run.stderr.strip()}&quot;)

Done when
- bash scripts/muse-exec.sh &quot;Summarize this repo&quot; prints the agent&#x27;s answer when muse is installed, and the install command when it isn&#x27;t.
- The README section covers install, first run, /login and META_API_KEY for CI.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,938<!-- --> class="docs-toc-panel" hidden=""></div></nav></div><p class="docs-p">Muse Code is Meta&#x27;s coding agent for the terminal and CI, built for <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/models#muse-spark">Muse Spark</a>. Run it in a project and it plans, edits, and runs commands to do a task, with approvals and an OS sandbox on from the first run.</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code and the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/overview">Model API</a> are two ways to use the same model. Call the API directly when you build your own agent or app. Run Muse Code when you want a ready-made coding agent at the command line or in a pipeline.</p><p class="docs-p"><a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows">Workflows</a> coordinate parallel and staged agent work when the installed build includes the workflow engine and the rollout is enabled. They are not available on every build or platform. <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging">Session messaging</a> lets independent live sessions exchange handoffs, review requests, and status updates.</p><h2 id="install" class="docs-h docs-h2">Install<a class="docs-anchor" href="#install" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Install Muse Code with the one-line installer. For a non-interactive environment such as <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#headless">CI</a>, set <code class="docs-code-inline">META_API_KEY</code> instead. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/auth">authentication and billing</a> for the full sign-in and billing setup flows.</p><h2 id="modes" class="docs-h docs-h2">Interactive or headless<a class="docs-anchor" href="#modes" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">The same binary runs two ways:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Interactive</strong>: <code class="docs-code-inline">muse</code> opens a terminal UI for a back-and-forth session with slash commands, approvals, and live status. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive">working with the agent</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Headless</strong>: <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec &quot;&lt;prompt&gt;&quot;</code> runs one prompt to completion for scripts and CI. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#headless">headless and CI</a>.</span></li></ul><h2 id="platforms" class="docs-h docs-h2">Platform support<a class="docs-anchor" href="#platforms" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows from one codebase. A few capabilities work differently on Windows:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>PowerShell replaces Bash.</strong> Agent-run commands use PowerShell syntax and Windows command-line tools.</span></li><li><span><strong>The sandbox may prompt for administrator approval.</strong> Windows can show a User Account Control (UAC) prompt the first time the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#sandbox">sandbox</a> initializes. Normal use does not require running as administrator.</span></li><li><span><strong>Voice input is unavailable</strong> on Windows. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#voice">voice input</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Session messaging is unavailable</strong> on Windows. It is supported on macOS and Linux. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging">session messaging</a>.</span></li></ul><h2 id="sdk" class="docs-h docs-h2">Drive it from your own program<a class="docs-anchor" href="#sdk" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Beyond the CLI, you can drive a Muse Code session from your own program over a stable, versioned session protocol. <code class="docs-code-inline">muse serve</code> runs the protocol, and <code class="docs-code-inline">muse schema</code> prints its JSON schema. The TypeScript SDK wraps the protocol: install it with <code class="docs-code-inline">npm install @muse-code/sdk</code>. A quickstart, cookbook recipes, and a generated API reference are in <a href="https://meta-models.github.io/muse-code-sdk" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">the Muse Code SDK docs<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</p><h2 id="whats-here" class="docs-h docs-h2">What to read next<a class="docs-anchor" href="#whats-here" aria-hidden="true" class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make this repository ready for Muse Code. Add scripts/muse-exec.sh that checks `muse --version` (printing the one-line install command for this OS when muse is missing), then runs `muse exec &quot;$@&quot;` from the repo root so any prompt can run headless. Add a short &quot;Using Muse Code&quot; section to the README: install, first run (`muse` in the repo, trust the workspace, sign in with the browser or an API key, `/login` to reopen it) and META_API_KEY for CI. Don&#x27;t install anything or sign in yourself.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Muse Code&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows PowerShell); confirm with `muse --version`.
- `muse` starts a session. The first run asks to trust the workspace (that loads its skills, rules and hooks) and to sign in with a browser or an API key.
- `muse exec &quot;&lt;prompt&gt;&quot;` runs one prompt to completion. Without a browser, Muse Code reads META_API_KEY (not MODEL_API_KEY).
- The default model is muse-spark-1.2; `--model` overrides it per run.
- On Windows agent commands use PowerShell, voice input and session messaging are unavailable, and the sandbox may show a UAC prompt once.
- Programs can drive a session with `muse serve` (`muse schema` prints the protocol&#x27;s JSON schema) or `npm install @muse-code/sdk`.

Starter code (Python)
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

# Run one Muse Code prompt headless; the agent&#x27;s output comes back on stdout.
if shutil.which(&quot;muse&quot;) is None:
    sys.exit(&quot;Install Muse Code: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh&quot;)

prompt = &quot; &quot;.join(sys.argv[1:]) or &quot;Summarize this repo.&quot;
run = subprocess.run([&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, prompt], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(run.stdout)
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec exited {run.returncode}: {run.stderr.strip()}&quot;)

Done when
- bash scripts/muse-exec.sh &quot;Summarize this repo&quot; prints the agent&#x27;s answer when muse is installed, and the install command when it isn&#x27;t.
- The README section covers install, first run, /login and META_API_KEY for CI.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,938<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
